items.why: The report gives flake 1 E2g at "1366.0" and flake 2 at "1368.84", an upshift of "+2.85 ± 0.25 cm-1". It notes broadening ("FWHM 18.8 ± 0.8 vs 15.5 ± 0.2") and says this fits "a thin, substrate-supported flake (1L or 2L)".
It cites "1L upshifted by typically 2-4 cm-1 (± 2)" and states "Position alone is not a layer-number criterion" and "Position-based layer assignment is unreliable".

It says "position is strain-dependent", mentions "random strain" via Gorbachev, and gives the 2L downshift of 1-2 cm-1. It never states that random strain from cleavage produces red shifts of about 1-2 cm-1, comparable in size to the monolayer upshift.

It reports flake 2's E2g as "about 12x weaker in peak height (about 10x in area)" under identical settings. It calls intensity "the better layer-number observable" and states "integrated E2g is proportional to N for the first few layers on a given substrate, but only after calibration".

It asks for AFM and for optical contrast ("green channel at about 530 nm" on 290 nm SiO2). It also requests a bare-Si spectrum so the Si-line intensity can serve as a reference, alongside an intensity calibration on the same stack.

wrong_claims.why: The report explicitly says "Raman cannot establish that flake 2 is a monolayer" and calls it "1L possible but unproven".

Following Cai, the summary asserts that the upshift "is the pattern reported for supported 1L/2L hBN" and that "1L and 2L are both compatible with 1368.8", treating 2L as upshifted. It does note that Gorbachev's 2L downshift "weighs against 2L".
